# nish/net/quic-packet

QUIC version 1's packets, as RFC 9000 §16-§17 frames them and RFC 9001 §5 protects them: the variable-length integer, the long and short headers, packet-number encoding and recovery, the Initial secrets, AEAD packet protection, header protection and the Retry integrity tag.

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { QuicHeader, QuicInitialSecrets, QuicKeys, QuicKeysSlot, QuicPacket, quicInitialSecrets,
         quicKeys, quicLongHeader, quicOpenPacket, quicParseHeader, quicSealPacket,
         QUIC_AEAD_AES_128_GCM, QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL, QUIC_PACKET_OK } from "nish/net/quic-packet"
import { Secret, secret, wipe } from "nish:secret"

const dcid: u8[] = [0x83, 0x94, 0xc8, 0xf0, 0x3e, 0x51, 0x57, 0x08]
const secrets: QuicInitialSecrets | null = quicInitialSecrets(dcid)   // RFC 9001 §5.2
if (secrets !== null) {
  const client: u8[] = new Array<u8>(32)                              // public, so a copy
  client.set(secrets.client)
  const held: Secret<u8[]> = secret(client)
  const slot: QuicKeysSlot = new QuicKeysSlot()                       // ours, so ours to wipe
  const keys: QuicKeys | null = quicKeys(slot, QUIC_AEAD_AES_128_GCM, held)
  wipe(held)
  const header: u8[] | null = quicLongHeader(QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL, dcid, [], [], 0, 4, 20)
  if (keys !== null && header !== null) {
    const datagram: u8[] | null = quicSealPacket(keys, header, 0, new Array<u8>(20))
    if (datagram !== null) {
      const parsed: QuicHeader = quicParseHeader(datagram, 0, 8)      // 8: our short DCID length
      const packet: QuicPacket = quicOpenPacket(keys, datagram, parsed, -1)
      if (packet.error === QUIC_PACKET_OK) {
        // packet.payload holds the 20 bytes of frames sealed above
      }
    }
  }
  slot.wipe()                                                         // once the level is done
}
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="quic​Decrypt​Packet" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicdecryptpacket">

Decrypts the payload of a packet whose header protection `quicRemoveHeaderProtection` took off (RFC 9001 §5.3), filling in `packet.payload` and setting `packet.error`: `QUIC_ERR_KEYS` for keys `quicKeys` did not make, `QUIC_ERR_DECRYPT` when it does not authenticate under `keys`, and `QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS` when it does but the header's reserved bits are not zero (RFC 9000 §17.2, §17.3.1), which the caller is to close the connection over.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Decrypt​Payload" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicdecryptpayload">

Decrypts the payload of the packet `header` describes, whose header in the clear `quicUnprotectHeader` answered as `clear` (RFC 9001 §5.3), without changing `datagram`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Initial​Secrets" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicinitialsecrets">

The secrets of RFC 9001 §5.2 for the client's first Destination Connection ID, `dcid`: `initial_secret` is HKDF-Extract under version 1's salt, and the client's and the server's are expanded from it with the labels `client in` and `server in`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Initial​Secrets​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicinitialsecretsinto">

`quicInitialSecrets` of the Destination Connection ID `buf[at .. at + length)`, read in place, into `client` and `server`, 32 bytes each.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Key​Update​Secret" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeyupdatesecret">

The next generation's traffic secret for a key update (RFC 9001 §6.1): HKDF-Expand-Label(`trafficSecret`, `quic ku`, "", Hash.length), taken and answered as a `Secret` the caller wipes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Key​Update​Secret​Held​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeyupdatesecretheldinto">

`quicKeyUpdateSecret` from one held secret into another (RFC 9001 §6.1): HKDF-Expand-Label(`src`, `quic ku`, "", Hash.length) written over `dst`'s bytes in place, under SHA-384 for a 48-byte secret and SHA-256 for a 32-byte one.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Key​Update​Secret​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeyupdatesecretinto">

`quicKeyUpdateSecret` into `out`, which must be exactly the secret's length and not `secret` itself.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeys">

The packet-protection keys of RFC 9001 §5.1 from a traffic secret, held as a `Secret` the caller still owns and wipes, derived into `slot`, which the caller owns too: the AEAD key (`quic key`), the IV (`quic iv`) and the header-protection key (`quic hp`), each HKDF-Expand-Label with an empty context under the hash `aead` pairs with, written into the slot's arrays and the AES schedules expanded there.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys​Held​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeysheldinto">

`quicKeysInto` from a traffic secret held as a `Secret`: the packet key, IV and header-protection key derived from it straight into the slot's arrays, the plain output of each derivation wiped, and the AES schedules expanded in place inside an arena block.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeysinto">

`quicKeys` into `slot`: the packet key, IV and header-protection key of RFC 9001 §5.1 derived from `secret` straight into the slot's arrays, in `kdf`, with the AES schedules expanded in place.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys​Update" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeysupdate">

The next generation's keys in a key update (RFC 9001 §6), derived into `slot`, which the caller owns and which must not be the slot `keys` live in: the packet key and IV from `nextSecret`, which `quicKeyUpdateSecret` made from the current secret and the caller still owns, read through a plain copy inside an arena block that is zeroed, and `keys`' header-protection key kept, since header protection never changes with the phase.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys​Update​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeysupdateinto">

`quicKeysUpdate` into `slot`, which must not be the slot `keys` live in: the next generation's packet key and IV from `nextSecret`, and `keys`' header-protection key shared, as every generation shares it (RFC 9001 §6).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Keys​Wipe" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quickeyswipe">

Zeroes every array `keys` holds: the packet key, the IV and the header-protection key with `secureZero`, and each AES schedule with `aesKeyWipe`, whose volatile stores reach the whole of `roundKeys` (the kernels' powers of H included) and H itself.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Long​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quiclongheader">

The unprotected long header of an Initial, 0-RTT or Handshake packet (RFC 9000 §17.2), ending with the packet number in `pnLength` bytes, for a payload of `payloadLength` bytes that `quicSealPacket` will protect.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Long​Header​Size" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quiclongheadersize">

The size of the long header `quicPutLongHeader` writes for these arguments, or 0 when it would refuse them (see `quicLongHeader`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Open​Packet" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicopenpacket">

Opens one packet of a datagram (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4): header protection off, the packet number recovered against `largestPn` (or -1), and the payload decrypted.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Packet​Copy" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicpacketcopy">

Writes `bytes[from .. from + length)` into `buf` at `at`; the caller has checked both windows.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Packet​Grow" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicpacketgrow">

Appends `count` zero bytes to `out`, which a writer then fills in place with the `put` form of what it appends: one encoder serves both.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Packet​Number​Decode" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicpacketnumberdecode">

The full packet number from the `pnLength`-byte `truncatedPn` on the wire, given `largestPn`, the largest packet number this endpoint has processed in that space, or -1 for none (RFC 9000 §17.1, §A.3): the one closest to `largestPn + 1` whose low bytes are `truncatedPn`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Packet​Number​Length" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicpacketnumberlength">

How many bytes to send packet number `fullPn` in (RFC 9000 §17.1, §A.2), when `largestAcked` is the largest the peer has acknowledged in its space, or -1 if none: enough that twice the unacknowledged range fits, 1 to 4.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Parse​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicparseheader">

Parses the header of the packet starting at `datagram[at]`, which is how a datagram of coalesced packets is walked: parse at 0, then at the answer's `end`, until `end` is the datagram's length (RFC 9000 §12.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Parse​Header​Into" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicparseheaderinto">

Parses the header of the packet starting at `datagram[at]` into `header`, filling only its numbers and the windows of its connection IDs and token (`dcidStart`, `dcidLength` and the rest), so nothing is copied or allocated: the form a connection reads every packet with.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Put​Long​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputlongheader">

Writes into `buf` at `at` the unprotected long header `quicLongHeader` answers, with the connection IDs the first `dcidLength` and `scidLength` bytes of `dcid` and `scid`, and answers the offset past it: where the payload goes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Put​Short​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputshortheader">

Writes into `buf` at `at` the unprotected short header `quicShortHeader` answers, with the Destination Connection ID the first `dcidLength` bytes of `dcid`, and answers the offset past it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Remove​Header​Protection" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicremoveheaderprotection">

Removes header protection from the packet `header` describes (RFC 9001 §5.4.1): the answer's `firstByte`, `pnLength`, `packetNumber`, `keyPhase` and `header` are filled in, the packet number recovered against `largestPn`, the largest this endpoint has processed in the packet's space (or -1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Retry​Integrity​Tag" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicretryintegritytag">

The Retry integrity tag of RFC 9001 §5.8: AES-128-GCM under version 1's fixed key and nonce over an empty plaintext, with the Retry pseudo-packet — `odcid`'s length and bytes, then the Retry packet up to its tag — as the associated data.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Retry​Packet" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicretrypacket">

A whole Retry packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.5, RFC 9001 §5.8): the long header with `unused` in the first byte's low four bits (the server picks them; mask them with randomness), the client's SCID as `dcid`, the server's new SCID, the address-validation `token`, and the integrity tag over `odcid`, the DCID the client's Initial was sent to.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Retry​Verify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicretryverify">

Whether the Retry `header` describes carries a valid integrity tag for `odcid`, the DCID of the Initial this client sent (RFC 9001 §5.8).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Seal​In​Place" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicsealinplace">

Protects one packet in place (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Seal​Packet" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicsealpacket">

Protects one packet (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4.1): `header` is what `quicLongHeader` or `quicShortHeader` built, ending with the packet number, and `packetNumber` is the full number its last bytes truncate.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Short​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicshortheader">

The unprotected short header of a 1-RTT packet (RFC 9000 §17.3.1): the first byte with the spin and key-phase bits, the Destination Connection ID and the packet number in `pnLength` bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Unprotect​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicunprotectheader">

Removes header protection from the packet `header` describes (RFC 9001 §5.4.1) without changing `datagram`: `packet`'s `error`, `firstByte`, `pnLength`, `packetNumber` and `keyPhase` are set, and the answer is the header in the clear, packet number included, which is the AEAD's associated data: empty when `error` is not `QUIC_PACKET_OK`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Length" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintlength">

The length of the variable-length integer whose first byte is at `bytes[at]`, read from its two-bit prefix: 1, 2, 4 or 8.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Push" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintpush">

Appends `value` to `out` as a variable-length integer in the fewest bytes (RFC 9000 §16).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Push​Sized" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintpushsized">

Appends `value` to `out` as a variable-length integer of exactly `size` bytes, as `quicVarintPut` writes it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Put" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintput">

Writes `value` into `buf[at .. at + size)` as a variable-length integer of exactly `size` bytes, which may be longer than it needs (RFC 9000 §16 allows that, and a Length field written before its packet is complete uses it).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Read" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintread">

The variable-length integer at `bytes[at]` (RFC 9000 §16, §A.1), read only from `bytes[at .. end)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quic​Varint​Size" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicvarintsize">

The bytes a variable-length integer needs (RFC 9000 §16): 1, 2, 4 or 8, or 0 for a value that has no encoding, below zero or past 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Header" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicheader">

One packet's header as `quicParseHeader` read it from a datagram.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Initial​Secrets" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicinitialsecrets-1">

The two Initial secrets RFC 9001 §5.2 derives from the client's first Destination Connection ID.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Keys" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quickeys-1">

One packet's protection keys (RFC 9001 §5.1): the AEAD's key and IV, and the header-protection key, all derived from one traffic secret by `quicKeys`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Keys​Slot" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quickeysslot">

The storage one direction of one level's packet keys lives in for a connection slot (QUIC-3): a key and a header-protection key of each length, the IV, and an AES key schedule of each size for each, made once, and the `QuicKeys` that `quicKeysInto` and `quicKeysUpdateInto` point at the ones the negotiated AEAD uses.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="Quic​Packet" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicpacket">

One packet with its protection removed by `quicOpenPacket`, or as far as that got.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="Sans-IO">

The module takes bytes in and gives bytes out, with no socket and no clock. It
frames and protects packets and stops there, so it knows nothing of frames,
of a connection's state or of which keys a level is on; that is
`nish/net/quic` (WP34 Q2). Only version 1 (`0x00000001`) is spoken. A long
header of another version is parsed as far as RFC 8999's invariants go,
which is what a server needs to send Version Negotiation, and reported as
`QUIC_ERR_VERSION`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**What a parse refuses.** Every read is bounds-checked against the datagram,
so nothing a peer sends can make this module panic.

A header that runs past the datagram is `QUIC_ERR_TRUNCATED`; a clear fixed
bit `QUIC_ERR_FIXED_BIT`; a connection ID over 20 bytes in a version 1 header
`QUIC_ERR_CID_LENGTH`; a Length field reaching past the datagram
`QUIC_ERR_LENGTH`; a packet too short to sample for header protection
`QUIC_ERR_SAMPLE`; a payload that does not authenticate `QUIC_ERR_DECRYPT`;
and nonzero reserved bits once both protections are off
`QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS`, which RFC 9000 §17.2 makes a connection error
rather than a drop, so the payload is still handed back with it. The
builders, whose inputs come from this side rather than from a peer, answer
`null` for an argument out of range.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="In place">

For a connection that allocates nothing per packet,
`quicParseHeaderInto` reads a header as windows into the datagram, the
`quicPut*` builders write a header into a caller's buffer, `quicSealInPlace`
seals a packet where it lies, and `quicUnprotectHeader` and
`quicDecryptPayload` open one storing only numbers into the `QuicPacket`
they are given. The AEADs allocate; `quicSealInPlace` releases what they
allocated before it answers, and the opening halves answer arrays the
caller releases, inside its own arena block.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Coalesced packets">

**Coalesced packets** (RFC 9000 §12.2) are split by length: a long header
carries its own Length, and `QuicHeader.end` is where the next packet in the
datagram starts. A short header has none, so it runs to the datagram's end.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

`QuicKeys` holds a packet key, an IV and a header-protection
key, pointing into a `QuicKeysSlot`'s arrays. `quicKeys` and `quicKeysUpdate`
take a traffic secret as a `Secret` from `nish:secret` and a slot the caller
owns, and derive into the slot; a slot the caller owns is the caller's to
wipe, and `QuicKeysSlot.wipe` zeroes it with stores no optimiser removes, AES
schedules included (QUIC-1). `quicKeyUpdateSecret` answers the next secret as
a `Secret`, and every derivation wipes its HKDF intermediates before it
returns. `quicKeysWipe` zeroes the arrays one `QuicKeys` points at.

The Initial keys are not secret, because anyone who reads the client's first
DCID can derive them (RFC 9001 §5.2), so `quicInitialSecrets` answers plain
arrays, and `quicKeysInto`, `quicKeysUpdateInto`, `quicKeyUpdateSecretInto`
and `quicInitialSecretsInto` derive from plain secrets over a caller's
`HkdfScratch`; the Handshake and 1-RTT keys are secret. Each derivation's own
temporaries go with its arena block. A slot whose traffic secret is held as a
`Secret` may also derive with `quicKeysHeldInto`, and ratchet the secret in
place with `quicKeyUpdateSecretHeldInto`. Sealing and opening a packet wipe
the nonce, which gives the IV away, and the header-protection mask once each
is used (QUIC-2).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Constant time">

The AEADs and the header-protection masks are
`nish/crypto/aes` and `nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305`, with their guarantees.
What this module branches on is public: lengths, the packet type, the
packet number once header protection is off (it is in the clear to anyone
who holds the header-protection key, and RFC 9001 §5.4.1 protects it against
observers, not timing), and whether a payload authenticated.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Provenance">

Written from RFC 9000 and RFC 9001, in this module's own structure: nothing
here is ported from another implementation. The packet-number decoding
follows the arithmetic of RFC 9000 §A.3 and the length choice the rule of
§A.2, neither line by line.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Private names">

They carry the `quicPacket` prefix because a `std/` module's
private functions share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

</scalar-detail>

## Functions

### quicDecryptPacket

Decrypts the payload of a packet whose header protection
`quicRemoveHeaderProtection` took off (RFC 9001 §5.3), filling in
`packet.payload` and setting `packet.error`: `QUIC_ERR_KEYS` for keys
`quicKeys` did not make, `QUIC_ERR_DECRYPT` when it does not authenticate
under `keys`, and `QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS` when it
does but the header's reserved bits are not zero (RFC 9000 §17.2, §17.3.1),
which the caller is to close the connection over. Answers whether the
payload authenticated. A packet already in error is left as it is.

```ts
function quicDecryptPacket(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
  packet: QuicPacket,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The packet's parsed header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packet" type="QuicPacket" required>

What `quicRemoveHeaderProtection` answered for this packet.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the payload authenticated, `QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS` included, so read
  `packet.error` too.

</scalar-field>

### quicDecryptPayload

Decrypts the payload of the packet `header` describes, whose header in the
clear `quicUnprotectHeader` answered as `clear` (RFC 9001 §5.3), without
changing `datagram`. Sets `packet.error` as `quicDecryptPacket` does and
answers the plaintext frames, or `null` when they did not authenticate
(or `packet` was already in error). Only numbers are stored into `packet`.

```ts
function quicDecryptPayload(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
  clear: u8[],
  packet: QuicPacket,
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The packet's parsed header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="clear" type="u8[]" required>

What `quicUnprotectHeader` answered for this packet: the AEAD's associated data.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packet" type="QuicPacket" required>

The result `quicUnprotectHeader` filled for this packet; only its `error` is changed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A new array holding the frames, also for `QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS`, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicInitialSecrets

The secrets of RFC 9001 §5.2 for the client's first Destination Connection
ID, `dcid`: `initial_secret` is HKDF-Extract under version 1's salt, and the
client's and the server's are expanded from it with the labels `client in`
and `server in`. Answers `null` for a `dcid` over 20 bytes.

```ts
function quicInitialSecrets(
  dcid: u8[],
): QuicInitialSecrets | null
```

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID of the client's first Initial, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicInitialSecrets | null">

The two 32-byte secrets as plain arrays, which are not secret, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicInitialSecretsInto

`quicInitialSecrets` of the Destination Connection ID `buf[at .. at +
length)`, read in place, into `client` and `server`, 32 bytes each.
Answers whether it derived: not for an ID over 20 bytes, a window outside
`buf`, or an output of another length.

```ts
function quicInitialSecretsInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  length: i32,
  client: u8[],
  server: u8[],
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, reused across derivations; its secret-bearing fields are wiped
  before each returns (its `info` label is not).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the client's first Destination Connection ID, such as the datagram.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `buf` where the ID starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

The ID's length in bytes, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="client" type="u8[]" required>

The 32-byte array `client_initial_secret` is written over.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="server" type="u8[]" required>

The 32-byte array `server_initial_secret` is written over.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when both secrets were written; false, both untouched, otherwise.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeyUpdateSecret

The next generation's traffic secret for a key update (RFC 9001 §6.1):
HKDF-Expand-Label(`trafficSecret`, `quic ku`, "", Hash.length), taken and
answered as a `Secret` the caller wipes. The header-protection key does
not change with it (§6), so the new keys are `quicKeysUpdate` of the old
keys and this. Answers `null` where `quicKeys` would.

```ts
function quicKeyUpdateSecret(
  aead: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]> | null
```

<scalar-field name="aead" type="i32" required>

The negotiated suite, one of the `QUIC_AEAD_*` constants.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The current generation's traffic secret; borrowed, and left for the caller to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt; | null">

The next generation's secret, a new `Secret` the caller owns and wipes, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeyUpdateSecretHeldInto

`quicKeyUpdateSecret` from one held secret into another (RFC 9001 §6.1):
HKDF-Expand-Label(`src`, `quic ku`, "", Hash.length) written over `dst`'s
bytes in place, under SHA-384 for a 48-byte secret and SHA-256 for a
32-byte one. `dst` may be `src`, which ratchets it. Answers whether it
derived: not unless both hold 32 bytes or both 48.

```ts
function quicKeyUpdateSecretHeldInto(
  dst: Secret<u8[]>,
  src: Secret<u8[]>,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="dst" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The secret overwritten with the next generation's; the caller's, and the caller wipes it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="src" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The current generation's secret; borrowed, and not wiped here unless it is `dst`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when `dst` holds the next secret; false, both untouched, for mismatched or wrong lengths.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeyUpdateSecretInto

`quicKeyUpdateSecret` into `out`, which must be exactly the secret's
length and not `secret` itself. Answers whether it derived, which it does
where `quicKeyUpdateSecret` answers a secret.

```ts
function quicKeyUpdateSecretInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  aead: i32,
  secret: u8[],
  out: u8[],
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, reused across derivations; its secret-bearing fields are wiped
  before each returns (its `info` label is not).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="aead" type="i32" required>

The negotiated suite, one of the `QUIC_AEAD_*` constants.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="secret" type="u8[]" required>

The current traffic secret as a plain array; only read, and not wiped.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array the next secret is written over, 32 bytes (48 for AES-256-GCM).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when `out` holds the next secret; false, `out` untouched, for a wrong length or `aead`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeys

The packet-protection keys of RFC 9001 §5.1 from a traffic secret, held as a
`Secret` the caller still owns and wipes, derived into `slot`, which the
caller owns too: the AEAD key (`quic key`), the IV (`quic iv`) and the
header-protection key (`quic hp`), each HKDF-Expand-Label with an empty
context under the hash `aead` pairs with, written into the slot's arrays and
the AES schedules expanded there.

The secret is read through a plain copy inside an arena block, which is
zeroed, and the derivation's temporaries go with the block, so the call keeps
in the arena only the `HkdfScratch` it makes for the derivation, which wipes
itself before the derivation returns. Answers the slot's keys, which the next
derivation into it overwrites and `QuicKeysSlot.wipe` zeroes, or `null`,
deriving nothing, for an `aead` this module does not know or a secret that is
not that hash's length. The Initial secrets are public (RFC 9001 §5.2), so a
caller deriving Initial keys wraps a copy of one in `secret`, or uses
`quicKeysInto`.

```ts
function quicKeys(
  slot: QuicKeysSlot,
  aead: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): QuicKeys | null
```

<scalar-field name="slot" type="QuicKeysSlot" required>

The caller's slot to derive into; its earlier keys are overwritten.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="aead" type="i32" required>

The negotiated suite, one of the `QUIC_AEAD_*` constants.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The level's traffic secret, 32 bytes (48 for AES-256-GCM); borrowed: it is
  not wiped here, and the caller wipes it once no more keys come from it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicKeys | null">

`slot.keys`, valid until the slot is derived into again or wiped, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeysHeldInto

`quicKeysInto` from a traffic secret held as a `Secret`: the packet key, IV
and header-protection key derived from it straight into the slot's arrays,
the plain output of each derivation wiped, and the AES schedules expanded
in place inside an arena block. Answers the slot's keys, or `null`,
deriving nothing, where `quicKeys` answers `null`.

```ts
function quicKeysHeldInto(
  slot: QuicKeysSlot,
  aead: i32,
  secret: Secret<u8[]>,
): QuicKeys | null
```

<scalar-field name="slot" type="QuicKeysSlot" required>

The caller's slot to derive into; its earlier keys are overwritten.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="aead" type="i32" required>

The negotiated suite, one of the `QUIC_AEAD_*` constants.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="secret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The traffic secret, 32 bytes (48 for AES-256-GCM); borrowed, and left for the caller to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicKeys | null">

`slot.keys`, valid until the slot is derived into again or wiped, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeysInto

`quicKeys` into `slot`: the packet key, IV and header-protection key of
RFC 9001 §5.1 derived from `secret` straight into the slot's arrays, in
`kdf`, with the AES schedules expanded in place. Answers the slot's keys,
or `null`, deriving nothing, where `quicKeys` answers `null`. The keys
are the slot's: the next derivation into it overwrites them.

```ts
function quicKeysInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  slot: QuicKeysSlot,
  aead: i32,
  secret: u8[],
): QuicKeys | null
```

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, reused across derivations; its secret-bearing fields are wiped
  before each returns (its `info` label is not).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="slot" type="QuicKeysSlot" required>

The caller's slot to derive into; its earlier keys are overwritten.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="aead" type="i32" required>

The negotiated suite, one of the `QUIC_AEAD_*` constants.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="secret" type="u8[]" required>

The traffic secret as a plain array, 32 bytes (48 for AES-256-GCM); only read, and not
  wiped, so a caller passing a non-Initial secret wipes it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicKeys | null">

`slot.keys`, valid until the slot is derived into again or wiped, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeysUpdate

The next generation's keys in a key update (RFC 9001 §6), derived into
`slot`, which the caller owns and which must not be the slot `keys` live in:
the packet key and IV from `nextSecret`, which `quicKeyUpdateSecret` made
from the current secret and the caller still owns, read through a plain copy
inside an arena block that is zeroed, and `keys`' header-protection key kept,
since header protection never changes with the phase.

The new generation holds its own copy of that key and its own schedule, in
the slot, so wiping one generation leaves the other usable. Answers the
slot's keys, or `null`, deriving nothing, for keys `quicKeys` did not make,
keys that live in `slot`, or a secret of the wrong length.

```ts
function quicKeysUpdate(
  slot: QuicKeysSlot,
  keys: QuicKeys,
  nextSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): QuicKeys | null
```

<scalar-field name="slot" type="QuicKeysSlot" required>

The caller's slot for the next generation; a different slot from the one `keys` live in.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The current generation's keys, whose header-protection key is copied; left unchanged.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nextSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The next generation's traffic secret; borrowed, and left for the caller to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicKeys | null">

`slot.keys`, valid until the slot is derived into again or wiped, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeysUpdateInto

`quicKeysUpdate` into `slot`, which must not be the slot `keys` live in:
the next generation's packet key and IV from `nextSecret`, and `keys`'
header-protection key shared, as every generation shares it (RFC 9001
§6). Answers the slot's keys, or `null` where `quicKeysUpdate` does.
Unlike `quicKeysUpdate` the header-protection key and its schedule are the
same arrays as `keys`', not a copy, so wiping either generation zeroes the
header-protection key both use.

```ts
function quicKeysUpdateInto(
  kdf: HkdfScratch,
  slot: QuicKeysSlot,
  keys: QuicKeys,
  nextSecret: u8[],
): QuicKeys | null
```

<scalar-field name="kdf" type="HkdfScratch" required>

The caller's HKDF scratch, reused across derivations; its secret-bearing fields are wiped
  before each returns (its `info` label is not).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="slot" type="QuicKeysSlot" required>

The caller's slot for the next generation; a different slot from the one `keys` live in.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The current generation's keys, whose header-protection arrays are shared; left unchanged.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nextSecret" type="u8[]" required>

The next generation's traffic secret as a plain array; only read, and not wiped.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicKeys | null">

`slot.keys`, valid until the slot is derived into again or wiped, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicKeysWipe

Zeroes every array `keys` holds: the packet key, the IV and the
header-protection key with `secureZero`, and each AES schedule with
`aesKeyWipe`, whose volatile stores reach the whole of `roundKeys` (the
kernels' powers of H included) and H itself. It zeroes the arrays `keys`
points at now; a slot's arrays of the other lengths are
`QuicKeysSlot.wipe`'s, which zeroes them all.

```ts
function quicKeysWipe(keys: QuicKeys): void
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The keys to zero. Nothing marks them wiped and nothing refuses them afterwards, so derive
  into them again before sealing or opening with them.

</scalar-field>

### quicLongHeader

The unprotected long header of an Initial, 0-RTT or Handshake packet
(RFC 9000 §17.2), ending with the packet number in `pnLength` bytes, for a
payload of `payloadLength` bytes that `quicSealPacket` will protect. The
Length field counts the packet number, the payload and the AEAD tag, and is
always written in two bytes (RFC 9000 §16 allows the longer form), so the
header's size does not move with the payload's and a caller padding a
packet to a size knows the header first. `token` goes in an Initial and
must be empty otherwise.

Answers `null` for another `type`, a connection ID over 20 bytes, a token
on a non-Initial packet, a `pnLength` outside 1 to 4, a packet number that
is not one, a negative `payloadLength`, or a Length past 16383, the most two
bytes hold and far more than a datagram carries.

```ts
function quicLongHeader(
  type: i32,
  dcid: u8[],
  scid: u8[],
  token: u8[],
  packetNumber: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
  payloadLength: i32,
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="type" type="i32" required>

`QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL`, `QUIC_PACKET_ZERO_RTT` or `QUIC_PACKET_HANDSHAKE`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scid" type="u8[]" required>

The Source Connection ID, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="token" type="u8[]" required>

An Initial's token, or empty.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1; its low `pnLength` bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payloadLength" type="i32" required>

The plaintext payload's length in bytes, without the AEAD tag.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A new array holding the header, or `null` for an argument out of range.

</scalar-field>

### quicLongHeaderSize

The size of the long header `quicPutLongHeader` writes for these
arguments, or 0 when it would refuse them (see `quicLongHeader`).

```ts
function quicLongHeaderSize(
  type: i32,
  dcidLength: i32,
  scidLength: i32,
  tokenLength: i32,
  packetNumber: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
  payloadLength: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="type" type="i32" required>

`QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL`, `QUIC_PACKET_ZERO_RTT` or `QUIC_PACKET_HANDSHAKE`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcidLength" type="i32" required>

The Destination Connection ID's length in bytes, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scidLength" type="i32" required>

The Source Connection ID's length in bytes, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="tokenLength" type="i32" required>

The token's length in bytes; 0 for anything but an Initial.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1; only range-checked, as the size does not
  depend on it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payloadLength" type="i32" required>

The plaintext payload's length in bytes, without the AEAD tag.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The header's length in bytes, packet number included, or 0 for an argument out of range.

</scalar-field>

### quicOpenPacket

Opens one packet of a datagram (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4): header protection
off, the packet number recovered against `largestPn` (or -1), and the
payload decrypted. The answer's `error` is `QUIC_PACKET_OK` with `payload`
holding the frames, or the `QUIC_ERR_*` of the step that failed — see
`quicRemoveHeaderProtection` and `quicDecryptPacket`.

```ts
function quicOpenPacket(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
  largestPn: i64,
): QuicPacket
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The packet's parsed header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="largestPn" type="i64" required>

The largest packet number processed in the packet's space, or -1 for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicPacket">

A new `QuicPacket`; read its `error` before any other field.

</scalar-field>

### quicPacketCopy

Writes `bytes[from .. from + length)` into `buf` at `at`; the caller has checked both windows.
A byte outside either window is skipped rather than written, so a wrong window cannot panic.

```ts
function quicPacketCopy(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  bytes: u8[],
  from: i32,
  length: i32,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into; it is not grown.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `buf` of the first byte written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to copy from.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="from" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `bytes` of the first byte copied.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes to copy.

</scalar-field>

### quicPacketGrow

Appends `count` zero bytes to `out`, which a writer then fills in place
with the `put` form of what it appends: one encoder serves both.

```ts
function quicPacketGrow(
  out: u8[],
  count: i32,
): void
```

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to lengthen.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="count" type="i32" required>

How many zero bytes to append; 0 or less appends none.

</scalar-field>

### quicPacketNumberDecode

The full packet number from the `pnLength`-byte `truncatedPn` on the wire,
given `largestPn`, the largest packet number this endpoint has processed in
that space, or -1 for none (RFC 9000 §17.1, §A.3): the one closest to
`largestPn + 1` whose low bytes are `truncatedPn`. Answers -1 when
`pnLength` is not 1 to 4 or `truncatedPn` does not fit in it.

```ts
function quicPacketNumberDecode(
  largestPn: i64,
  truncatedPn: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
): i64
```

<scalar-field name="largestPn" type="i64" required>

The largest packet number processed in this space, or -1 for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="truncatedPn" type="i64" required>

The packet number's low bytes as the header carried them, below 2^(8 × `pnLength`).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i64">

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1, or -1 for an argument out of range.

</scalar-field>

### quicPacketNumberLength

How many bytes to send packet number `fullPn` in (RFC 9000 §17.1, §A.2),
when `largestAcked` is the largest the peer has acknowledged in its space,
or -1 if none: enough that twice the unacknowledged range fits, 1 to 4.
Answers 0 when no length will do — `fullPn` not above `largestAcked`, not a
packet number, or more than 2^31 packets unacknowledged.

```ts
function quicPacketNumberLength(
  fullPn: i64,
  largestAcked: i64,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="fullPn" type="i64" required>

The packet number about to be sent, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="largestAcked" type="i64" required>

The largest packet number the peer has acknowledged in this space, or -1 for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The packet-number length in bytes, 1 to 4, or 0 when none will do.

</scalar-field>

### quicParseHeader

Parses the header of the packet starting at `datagram[at]`, which is how a
datagram of coalesced packets is walked: parse at 0, then at the answer's
`end`, until `end` is the datagram's length (RFC 9000 §12.2).
`shortDcidLength` is the length of the connection IDs this endpoint hands
out, which is the only way to know where a short header's DCID ends
(RFC 9000 §17.3.1); one outside 0 to 20 reads as `QUIC_ERR_TRUNCATED`.
The connection IDs, the token and a Retry's tag are copied out into the
answer's arrays; `quicParseHeaderInto` reads the same without a copy.

The answer's `error` says what stopped it; nothing a peer sends panics.

```ts
function quicParseHeader(
  datagram: u8[],
  at: i32,
  shortDcidLength: i32,
): QuicHeader
```

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes, only read; the datagram runs to the array's end.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset where the packet starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="shortDcidLength" type="i32" required>

The length in bytes of the connection IDs this endpoint hands out, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicHeader">

A new `QuicHeader`; read its `error` before any other field.

</scalar-field>

### quicParseHeaderInto

Parses the header of the packet starting at `datagram[at]` into `header`,
filling only its numbers and the windows of its connection IDs and token
(`dcidStart`, `dcidLength` and the rest), so nothing is copied or
allocated: the form a connection reads every packet with. Answers
`header.error`. Every field is reset first, so one `QuicHeader` serves
every packet; its `dcid`, `scid`, `token` and `retryTag` arrays are left
as they were. The datagram is `datagram[at .. limit)`, so one buffer can
hold several (a GRO receive); a `limit` past the array reads as its length.
See `quicParseHeader` for what is read and refused.

```ts
function quicParseHeaderInto(
  header: QuicHeader,
  datagram: u8[],
  at: i32,
  limit: i32,
  shortDcidLength: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The header to overwrite; its windows index into `datagram`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset where the packet starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="limit" type="i32" required>

The byte offset one past the datagram's end.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="shortDcidLength" type="i32" required>

The length in bytes of the connection IDs this endpoint hands out, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

`QUIC_PACKET_OK`, or the `QUIC_ERR_*` that stopped the parse.

</scalar-field>

### quicPutLongHeader

Writes into `buf` at `at` the unprotected long header `quicLongHeader`
answers, with the connection IDs the first `dcidLength` and `scidLength`
bytes of `dcid` and `scid`, and answers the offset past it: where the
payload goes. Answers -1, writing nothing, where `quicLongHeader` answers
`null`, and for a header that does not fit in `buf` from `at`.

```ts
function quicPutLongHeader(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  type: i32,
  dcid: u8[],
  dcidLength: i32,
  scid: u8[],
  scidLength: i32,
  token: u8[],
  packetNumber: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
  payloadLength: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into; it is not grown.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `buf` where the packet starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="type" type="i32" required>

`QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL`, `QUIC_PACKET_ZERO_RTT` or `QUIC_PACKET_HANDSHAKE`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the Destination Connection ID at their start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcidLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes of `dcid` are the ID, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scid" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the Source Connection ID at their start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scidLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes of `scid` are the ID, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="token" type="u8[]" required>

The whole of an Initial's token; empty for the other types.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1; its low `pnLength` bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payloadLength" type="i32" required>

The plaintext payload's length in bytes, without the AEAD tag.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The byte offset one past the packet number, where the payload goes, or -1 when nothing was
  written.

</scalar-field>

### quicPutShortHeader

Writes into `buf` at `at` the unprotected short header `quicShortHeader`
answers, with the Destination Connection ID the first `dcidLength` bytes of
`dcid`, and answers the offset past it. Answers -1, writing nothing, where
`quicShortHeader` answers `null`, and for a header that does not fit.

```ts
function quicPutShortHeader(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  dcid: u8[],
  dcidLength: i32,
  spin: boolean,
  keyPhase: boolean,
  packetNumber: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into; it is not grown.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `buf` where the packet starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the Destination Connection ID at their start.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="dcidLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes of `dcid` are the ID, 0 to 20.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="spin" type="boolean" required>

The latency spin bit (RFC 9000 §17.4).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="keyPhase" type="boolean" required>

The Key Phase bit, which says which generation of 1-RTT keys protects the packet
  (RFC 9001 §6).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1; its low `pnLength` bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The byte offset one past the packet number, where the payload goes, or -1 when nothing was
  written.

</scalar-field>

### quicRemoveHeaderProtection

Removes header protection from the packet `header` describes (RFC 9001
§5.4.1): the answer's `firstByte`, `pnLength`, `packetNumber`, `keyPhase`
and `header` are filled in, the packet number recovered against
`largestPn`, the largest this endpoint has processed in the packet's space
(or -1). The header-protection key never changes with a key update, so a
caller holding two generations of keys calls this, reads `keyPhase`, and
hands the answer to `quicDecryptPacket` with the generation it names
(RFC 9001 §6.3).

`error` is the header's own for a header that did not parse,
`QUIC_ERR_NOT_PROTECTED` for a Retry, `QUIC_ERR_KEYS` for keys `quicKeys`
did not make, and `QUIC_ERR_SAMPLE` for a packet too short to sample.

```ts
function quicRemoveHeaderProtection(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
  largestPn: i64,
): QuicPacket
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys; the whole set must be usable, though only the header-protection key is used.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The packet's parsed header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="largestPn" type="i64" required>

The largest packet number processed in the packet's space, or -1 for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicPacket">

A new `QuicPacket` with no payload yet; read its `error` before any other field.

</scalar-field>

### quicRetryIntegrityTag

The Retry integrity tag of RFC 9001 §5.8: AES-128-GCM under version 1's
fixed key and nonce over an empty plaintext, with the Retry pseudo-packet —
`odcid`'s length and bytes, then the Retry packet up to its tag — as the
associated data. `odcid` is the Destination Connection ID of the client's
Initial the Retry answers. Answers `null` for an `odcid` over 20 bytes.

```ts
function quicRetryIntegrityTag(
  odcid: u8[],
  retryWithoutTag: u8[],
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="odcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID of the client's first Initial, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="retryWithoutTag" type="u8[]" required>

The Retry packet from its first byte to just before the tag, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

The 16-byte tag as a new array, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicRetryPacket

A whole Retry packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.5, RFC 9001 §5.8): the long header with
`unused` in the first byte's low four bits (the server picks them; mask
them with randomness), the client's SCID as `dcid`, the server's new SCID,
the address-validation `token`, and the integrity tag over `odcid`, the
DCID the client's Initial was sent to. Answers `null` for a connection ID
over 20 bytes, an empty token (a client discards that Retry, §17.2.5.2) or
`unused` outside 0 to 15.

```ts
function quicRetryPacket(
  dcid: u8[],
  scid: u8[],
  token: u8[],
  odcid: u8[],
  unused: i32,
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The client's Source Connection ID, which the Retry is sent to; 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scid" type="u8[]" required>

The server's new Source Connection ID, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="token" type="u8[]" required>

The address-validation token the client is to echo; at least one byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="odcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID of the client's first Initial, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="unused" type="i32" required>

The first byte's four low bits, 0 to 15.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A new array holding the whole Retry, tag included, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicRetryVerify

Whether the Retry `header` describes carries a valid integrity tag for
`odcid`, the DCID of the Initial this client sent (RFC 9001 §5.8). The tag
is recomputed over the datagram's bytes and compared in constant time.
Answers `false` for a header that is not a Retry that parsed.

```ts
function quicRetryVerify(
  odcid: u8[],
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="odcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID of the Initial this client sent.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The Retry's header from `quicParseHeader`, which copies out `retryTag`;
  `quicParseHeaderInto` leaves that array as it was.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the integrity tag is valid for `odcid`: the packet was not altered and answers the
  Initial that carried that DCID. It authenticates nothing more (RFC 9001 §5.8).

</scalar-field>

### quicSealInPlace

Protects one packet in place (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4.1). `buf[start ..
start + headerLength)` is a header `quicPutLongHeader` or
`quicPutShortHeader` wrote, ending with the packet number, and the
`payloadLength` bytes after it are the frames; `packetNumber` is the full
number the header's last bytes truncate. The payload is sealed where it
lies, its tag written after it, and header protection put on: the answer
is the offset past the tag, which is where the packet ends, or -1, with
`buf` not to be sent, for anything `quicSealPacket` refuses and for a tag
that does not fit in `buf`. The AEAD's temporaries are released before it
answers, so sealing allocates nothing that outlives the call.

```ts
function quicSealInPlace(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  buf: u8[],
  start: i32,
  headerLength: i32,
  payloadLength: i32,
  packetNumber: i64,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer holding the packet; it is not grown, so it needs 16 bytes of room past the payload.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="start" type="i32" required>

The byte offset in `buf` where the packet starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="headerLength" type="i32" required>

The header's length in bytes, packet number included.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payloadLength" type="i32" required>

The plaintext payload's length in bytes; with the packet number, at least 4.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number the header carries, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The byte offset one past the AEAD tag, or -1 when the packet is not to be sent.

</scalar-field>

### quicSealPacket

Protects one packet (RFC 9001 §5.3, §5.4.1): `header` is what
`quicLongHeader` or `quicShortHeader` built, ending with the packet number,
and `packetNumber` is the full number its last bytes truncate. The answer
is the header under header protection followed by the AEAD-sealed payload
and its tag, ready to send or to coalesce; `quicSealInPlace` does the same
in a caller's buffer.

The header and the arguments are held to each other, because a packet that
disagrees with its own header is one the peer silently drops: the header's
packet-number bytes must be `packetNumber`'s low bytes, and a long header's
two-byte Length must count this `payload`. The sample is the 16 bytes from
4 past the packet number's start, so the packet number and payload together
must be at least 4 bytes; a shorter payload has to be padded first (RFC 9001
§5.4.2). Answers `null` for any of those, for a header too short for its
packet-number length, and for keys `quicKeys` did not make.

```ts
function quicSealPacket(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  header: u8[],
  packetNumber: i64,
  payload: u8[],
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="u8[]" required>

The unprotected header, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number the header carries, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payload" type="u8[]" required>

The plaintext frames, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A new array holding the protected packet, 16 bytes longer than header and payload, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

### quicShortHeader

The unprotected short header of a 1-RTT packet (RFC 9000 §17.3.1): the
first byte with the spin and key-phase bits, the Destination Connection ID
and the packet number in `pnLength` bytes. Answers `null` for a connection
ID over 20 bytes, a `pnLength` outside 1 to 4 or a packet number that is
not one.

```ts
function quicShortHeader(
  dcid: u8[],
  spin: boolean,
  keyPhase: boolean,
  packetNumber: i64,
  pnLength: i32,
): u8[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="dcid" type="u8[]" required>

The Destination Connection ID, 0 to 20 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="spin" type="boolean" required>

The latency spin bit (RFC 9000 §17.4).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="keyPhase" type="boolean" required>

The Key Phase bit, which says which generation of 1-RTT keys protects the packet
  (RFC 9001 §6).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetNumber" type="i64" required>

The full packet number, 0 to 2^62 - 1; its low `pnLength` bytes are written.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="pnLength" type="i32" required>

The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A new array holding the header, or `null` for an argument out of range.

</scalar-field>

### quicUnprotectHeader

Removes header protection from the packet `header` describes (RFC 9001
§5.4.1) without changing `datagram`: `packet`'s `error`, `firstByte`,
`pnLength`, `packetNumber` and `keyPhase` are set, and the answer is the
header in the clear, packet number included, which is the AEAD's
associated data: empty when `error` is not `QUIC_PACKET_OK`. Only numbers
are stored into `packet`, so a connection reuses one for every packet and
the answer is its own to let go. See `quicRemoveHeaderProtection`.

```ts
function quicUnprotectHeader(
  keys: QuicKeys,
  datagram: u8[],
  header: QuicHeader,
  largestPn: i64,
  packet: QuicPacket,
): u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="keys" type="QuicKeys" required>

The level's keys, as `quicKeys` or one of its `Into` forms made them.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="datagram" type="u8[]" required>

The received bytes `header` was parsed from, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="header" type="QuicHeader" required>

The packet's parsed header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="largestPn" type="i64" required>

The largest packet number processed in the packet's space, or -1 for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packet" type="QuicPacket" required>

The result to overwrite; its `header` and `payload` arrays are not touched.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

A new array holding the header in the clear, or an empty one when `packet.error` is set.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintLength

The length of the variable-length integer whose first byte is at
`bytes[at]`, read from its two-bit prefix: 1, 2, 4 or 8. Answers 0 when
`at` is outside `bytes`.

```ts
function quicVarintLength(
  bytes: u8[],
  at: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the integer.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset of the integer's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The integer's length in bytes, which may run past the end of `bytes`; or 0.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintPush

Appends `value` to `out` as a variable-length integer in the fewest bytes
(RFC 9000 §16). Answers `false`, appending nothing, for a value below zero
or past 2^62 - 1.

```ts
function quicVarintPush(
  out: u8[],
  value: i64,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to append to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="value" type="i64" required>

The integer, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the integer was appended.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintPushSized

Appends `value` to `out` as a variable-length integer of exactly `size`
bytes, as `quicVarintPut` writes it. Answers `false`, appending nothing,
when `size` is not 1, 2, 4 or 8 or is too short for `value`.

```ts
function quicVarintPushSized(
  out: u8[],
  value: i64,
  size: i32,
): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to append to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="value" type="i64" required>

The integer, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="size" type="i32" required>

The encoded length in bytes: 1, 2, 4 or 8, at least `quicVarintSize(value)`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the integer was appended.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintPut

Writes `value` into `buf[at .. at + size)` as a variable-length integer of
exactly `size` bytes, which may be longer than it needs (RFC 9000 §16
allows that, and a Length field written before its packet is complete uses
it). Answers `at + size`, or -1, writing nothing, when `size` is not 1, 2,
4 or 8, is too short for `value`, or does not fit in `buf` from `at`.

```ts
function quicVarintPut(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  value: i64,
  size: i32,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into; it is not grown.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset of the integer's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="value" type="i64" required>

The integer, 0 to 2^62 - 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="size" type="i32" required>

The encoded length in bytes: 1, 2, 4 or 8, at least `quicVarintSize(value)`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The byte offset one past the integer, or -1 when nothing was written.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintRead

The variable-length integer at `bytes[at]` (RFC 9000 §16, §A.1), read only
from `bytes[at .. end)`. Answers -1, which no varint holds, when it does not
fit in that window or the window is not inside `bytes`. Advance past it by
`quicVarintLength(bytes, at)`.

```ts
function quicVarintRead(
  bytes: u8[],
  at: i32,
  end: i32,
): i64
```

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes holding the integer.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The byte offset of the integer's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="end" type="i32" required>

The byte offset the integer must end at or before, at most `bytes.length`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i64">

The integer, 0 to 2^62 - 1, or -1 when it cannot be read.

</scalar-field>

### quicVarintSize

The bytes a variable-length integer needs (RFC 9000 §16): 1, 2, 4 or 8, or
0 for a value that has no encoding, below zero or past 2^62 - 1.

```ts
function quicVarintSize(value: i64): i32
```

<scalar-field name="value" type="i64" required>

The integer to encode.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The encoded length in bytes, or 0 when `value` has no encoding.

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### QuicHeader

One packet's header as `quicParseHeader` read it from a datagram. The
fields after `error` are meaningful as far as the parse got: all of them
when `error` is `QUIC_PACKET_OK`, and `version`, `dcid` and `scid` for
`QUIC_ERR_VERSION`, which is what Version Negotiation needs.

The packet number and the low bits of the first byte are still under
header protection here, so the header carries where they are rather than
what they hold; `quicOpenPacket` reads them.

```ts
class QuicHeader
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicHeader()` | Makes an empty header, every array empty and every window at 0, for `quicParseHeader` or `quicParseHeaderInto` to fill. |
| `dcid: u8[]` | The Destination Connection ID. |
| `dcidLength: i32` | The Destination Connection ID's length in bytes, 0 to 20; a short header's is the length the reader passed. |
| `dcidStart: i32` | Where `dcid`, `scid` and `token` sit in the datagram, as far as the parse got. `quicParseHeaderInto` fills these and nothing else, so a connection reads a header with no copy; `quicParseHeader` copies the windows out into the arrays above. |
| `end: i32` | One past the packet's last byte, which is where the next coalesced packet starts. |
| `error: i32` | `QUIC_PACKET_OK`, or the `QUIC_ERR_*` that stopped the parse. |
| `pnOffset: i32` | Where the protected packet number starts: the header-protection sample starts 4 bytes after it. For a Retry, which has none, where its tag starts. |
| `retryTag: u8[]` | A Retry's integrity tag, the datagram's last 16 bytes; empty for every other type. |
| `scid: u8[]` | The Source Connection ID; empty for a short header. |
| `scidLength: i32` | The Source Connection ID's length in bytes, 0 to 20; 0 for a short header. |
| `scidStart: i32` | Where the Source Connection ID starts in the datagram; 0 for a short header. |
| `start: i32` | Where in the datagram the packet starts. |
| `token: u8[]` | An Initial's token, or a Retry's; empty for every other type. |
| `tokenLength: i32` | An Initial's or a Retry's token length in bytes; 0 for every other type. |
| `tokenStart: i32` | Where an Initial's or a Retry's token starts in the datagram; 0 for every other type. |
| `type: i32` | `QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL`, `_ZERO_RTT`, `_HANDSHAKE`, `_RETRY` or `_SHORT`. |
| `version: i64` | The long header's 32-bit version, held in an `i64`; 0 for a short header, which has none. |

### QuicInitialSecrets

The two Initial secrets RFC 9001 §5.2 derives from the client's first Destination Connection ID.

```ts
class QuicInitialSecrets
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicInitialSecrets(client: u8[], server: u8[])` | Pairs two secrets already derived, keeping the arrays rather than copying them. |
| `client: u8[]` | `client_initial_secret`: what protects the client's Initial packets. |
| `server: u8[]` | `server_initial_secret`: what protects the server's. |

### QuicKeys

One packet's protection keys (RFC 9001 §5.1): the AEAD's key and IV, and
the header-protection key, all derived from one traffic secret by
`quicKeys`. For the AES suites the two keys are also kept expanded, so a
connection expands them once rather than once a packet.

```ts
class QuicKeys
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicKeys(aead: i32, key: u8[], iv: u8[], hp: u8[])` | Wraps keys already derived; the arrays are kept, not copied, so they stay the owner's to wipe. `packetAes` and `hpAes` start `null`; the `quicKeys*` functions fill them for the AES suites. A `QuicKeys` built by hand for an AES suite stays unusable: opening refuses it with `QUIC_ERR_KEYS`, and sealing answers `null`. |
| `aead: i32` | `QUIC_AEAD_AES_128_GCM`, `_AES_256_GCM` or `_CHACHA20_POLY1305`. |
| `hp: u8[]` | The header-protection key, the same length as `key`. |
| `hpAes: AesKey \| null` | `hp` expanded, for the AES suites; `null` for ChaCha20-Poly1305. |
| `iv: u8[]` | The 12-byte IV the packet number is XORed into. |
| `key: u8[]` | The packet-protection key: 16 bytes for AES-128-GCM, 32 for the others. |
| `packetAes: AesKey \| null` | `key` expanded, for the AES suites; `null` for ChaCha20-Poly1305. |

### QuicKeysSlot

The storage one direction of one level's packet keys lives in for a
connection slot (QUIC-3): a key and a header-protection key of each
length, the IV, and an AES key schedule of each size for each, made once,
and the `QuicKeys` that `quicKeysInto` and `quicKeysUpdateInto` point at
the ones the negotiated AEAD uses. So installing a level's keys, or a key
update's, writes into memory the slot already holds and keeps nothing in
the arena. The slot is its owner's to wipe (QUIC-1): `wipe` zeroes all of
it.

```ts
class QuicKeysSlot
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicKeysSlot()` | Makes the slot's arrays and key schedules once, with no keys derived yet (`keys.aead` is 0). |
| `hp128: AesKey` | The AES-128 key schedule for header protection, expanded from `hp16`. |
| `hp16: u8[]` | The 16-byte header-protection key an AES-128-GCM suite uses. |
| `hp256: AesKey` | The AES-256 key schedule for header protection, expanded from `hp32`. |
| `hp32: u8[]` | The 32-byte header-protection key an AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 suite uses. |
| `key16: u8[]` | The 16-byte packet key an AES-128-GCM suite uses. |
| `key32: u8[]` | The 32-byte packet key an AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 suite uses. |
| `keys: QuicKeys` | The keys, pointing into the arrays below; `aead` is 0 until something is derived. |
| `packet128: AesKey` | The AES-128 key schedule for packet protection, expanded from `key16`. |
| `packet256: AesKey` | The AES-256 key schedule for packet protection, expanded from `key32`. |
| `wipe(): void` | Zeroes every key the slot holds: the keys and the IV with `secureZero`, and each AES schedule with `aesKeyWipe`, whose volatile stores reach the whole of `roundKeys` (the kernels' powers of H included) and H itself. |

### QuicPacket

One packet with its protection removed by `quicOpenPacket`, or as far as
that got. With `error` at `QUIC_PACKET_OK` or `QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS`
every field is filled in; with `QUIC_ERR_DECRYPT` all but `payload`.

```ts
class QuicPacket
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicPacket()` | Makes an empty packet, its header and payload empty, for `quicOpenPacket` to fill. |
| `error: i32` | `QUIC_PACKET_OK`, or the `QUIC_ERR_*` that stopped the open. |
| `firstByte: i32` | The first byte with header protection removed. |
| `header: u8[]` | The header in the clear, packet number included: the AEAD's associated data. |
| `keyPhase: boolean` | A short header's Key Phase bit (RFC 9001 §6); `false` for a long header. |
| `packetNumber: i64` | The full packet number, recovered from the truncated one (RFC 9000 §17.1). |
| `payload: u8[]` | The decrypted frames. |
| `pnLength: i32` | The packet number's length on the wire, 1 to 4 bytes. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="20" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_MAX_CID_LENGTH: i32`

The longest connection ID version 1 allows (RFC 9000 §17.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="QUIC_​MAX_​VARINT" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_MAX_VARINT: i64`

The largest value a variable-length integer holds, 2^62 - 1 (RFC 9000 §16),
and so the largest packet number. Spelled as 2^30 × 2^32 - 1 because an
`i64` literal past 2^53 is refused (`docs/LANGUAGE.md`, numeric literals).

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_AEAD_AES_128_GCM: i32`

AEAD_AES_128_GCM with SHA-256, the Initial packets' AEAD (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_AEAD_AES_256_GCM: i32`

AEAD_AES_256_GCM with SHA-384 (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_AEAD_CHACHA20_POLY1305: i32`

AEAD_CHACHA20_POLY1305 with SHA-256 (TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_AEAD_TAG_SIZE: i32`

Every version 1 AEAD's tag, and so what each protected payload adds, in bytes (RFC 9001 §5.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_CID_LENGTH: i32`

A version 1 connection ID longer than 20 bytes (RFC 9000 §17.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_DECRYPT: i32`

The payload does not authenticate under the keys given (RFC 9001 §5.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_FIXED_BIT: i32`

The fixed bit, 0x40 of the first byte, is clear (RFC 9000 §17.2, §17.3.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_KEYS: i32`

Keys `quicKeys` or `quicKeysUpdate` did not make: a caller's own mistake, never a peer's.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_LENGTH: i32`

A long header whose Length field reaches past the end of the datagram (RFC 9000 §17.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_NOT_PROTECTED: i32`

The packet carries no protected payload: a Retry (RFC 9000 §17.2.5).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_RESERVED_BITS: i32`

The payload authenticated but a reserved bit is set, a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (RFC 9000 §17.2, §17.3.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_SAMPLE: i32`

Too few bytes after the packet number's offset to take the 16-byte sample (RFC 9001 §5.4.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_TRUNCATED: i32`

The header runs past the end of the datagram.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERR_VERSION: i32`

A long header of a version other than 1; `version`, `dcid` and `scid` are still filled in (RFC 8999 §5.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_HANDSHAKE: i32`

A long-header Handshake packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.4).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_INITIAL: i32`

A long-header Initial packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_OK: i32`

A packet parsed, or opened, with nothing wrong.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_RETRY: i32`

A long-header Retry packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.5).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_SHORT: i32`

A short-header, 1-RTT packet (RFC 9000 §17.3.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PACKET_ZERO_RTT: i32`

A long-header 0-RTT packet (RFC 9000 §17.2.3): parsed, since a server may be sent one; `quicLongHeader` builds one for a client.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RETRY_TAG_SIZE: i32`

The Retry integrity tag, in bytes (RFC 9001 §5.8).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SAMPLE_SIZE: i32`

The bytes of ciphertext header protection samples (RFC 9001 §5.4.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_VERSION_1: i64`

QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000 §15), the only version this module protects.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
